english: Homage to the giver of knowledge: in this chapter the Lord gathers into one place what was taught scattered, the jñāna (means to knowledge) set out through the end of the sixth chapter, the jñeya (the knowable, the nature of Brahman) set out in the six chapters from the seventh, the kṣetra (field) set out at 7.4, and the difference of puruṣa (persons) set out at 2.12, and having gathered them He sets each apart so that the topics stay unmixed. So He begins: this body, Kaunteya, is called kṣetra, and the one who knows it, those who know these matters call kṣetrajña (knower of the field).
divergence_note: Read with Jayatīrtha's Prameyadīpikā on Madhva's bhāṣya (their 13.2): Madhva supplies only a salutation and a one-line statement of method: the chapter gathers (piṇḍīkṛtya) and then separates (viviktya) four topics taught earlier. Jayatīrtha supplies the content of that line: he locates each topic in the earlier chapters, and identifies the puruṣa (person) topic as puruṣa-bheda (the difference of persons) taught at 2.12, so the chapter is framed from its first verse as restating difference, not as moving toward identity. The rest of his note is grammatical and expository: the absolutive in piṇḍīkṛtya is figurative (gauṇa), meaning 'for the sake of gathering', and viviktya is added because gathering alone would mix the topics and defeat understanding, so it means keeping each topic pure (prakaraṇa-śuddhi). Neither commentator glosses kṣetra, kṣetrajña or tad-vidaḥ, so the verse itself is rendered literally and no Dvaita doctrine of the body is claimed for it. Where Advaita and Advaita-bhakti point this hexad toward the knower being the one non-dual self, and Viśiṣṭādvaita reads the body as a mode of the self, the Dvaita frame here is structural: gather what was scattered, then keep it distinct, with the plurality of persons named as one of the things kept distinct.
everyday_application: Before a hard decision, pull together everything relevant that is lying in different places, then sort it back into separate piles so that gathering does not turn into blurring. A manager preparing a quarterly review can put customer complaints, engineering limits and budget into one document and still keep them in labeled sections, because a merged summary where the three bleed into each other helps nobody decide anything.
